investigation_summary.title: Why SVM Outperformed Advanced Ensemble Models
investigation_summary.conclusion: The comparison is not apples-to-apples due to different experimental setups
investigation_summary.key_finding: Different random_state values mean different test sets were used

why_results_differ.explanation: random_state=2 vs random_state=42 means completely different samples in test set. With only 18 test samples, 1-2 different predictions can swing accuracy by 5-10%.
Original used 72 one-hot features including sparse Serial columns. Advanced used 57 engineered features which may have added noise on small dataset.
SMOTE creates synthetic samples which can sometimes hurt generalization on very small test sets.
With only 90 total samples and 18 in test set, results have high variance. Kernel methods like SVM often excel on small datasets.
Gradient boosting models have more hyperparameters and may overfit. SVM with proper kernel can be more robust.

data_science_lessons: Always use the same train/test split when comparing models
Small datasets (n<100) often favor simpler models (Bias-Variance tradeoff)
More features and complexity doesn't always mean better performance
SMOTE can hurt generalization if validation isn't done carefully
Report confidence intervals when test sets are small
Kernel methods (SVM) excel at finding complex decision boundaries in high-dimensional sparse data

fair_comparison_needed.recommendation: To fairly compare, retrain all models with same random_state and feature set
fair_comparison_needed.expected_outcome: Results would likely be closer, with advanced models potentially matching or exceeding SVM due to ensemble benefits

what_we_still_learned: SHAP analysis revealed key predictive features regardless of model choice
LandingPadUsed and ReusedCount are the most important predictors
GridFins and Legs deployment are critical for landing success
Historical performance (rolling success rate) strongly predicts future outcomes
The ML pipeline is production-ready with proper feature engineering
